outcome: neonatal outcome (Apgar score <7, meconium-stained liquor, NICU admission)
cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women with singleton cephalic pregnancies, gestational age 37.1-42 weeks, in spontaneous or induced labor in the first stage active phase with cervical dilatation <= 8 cms.
finding: The study favors the use of the WHO modified partograph for better maternal and perinatal outcomes, noting a statistically significant difference in NICU admission rates between normal delivery and LSCS groups.
mod_finding: The majority of participants delivered vaginally (78%), with the remainder requiring Lower Segment Caesarean Section (22%), and NICU admission was statistically highly significant between normal delivery and LSCS groups (P=<0.0001).
